## Direct answer

A person detained without trial has the right to be informed of the grounds of their arrest and to consult a legal practitioner of their choice [Source 1] [Source 2].

A person detained without trial must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of their arrest [Source 1] [Source 2].

## Why this is the legal position

- Article 22(1) of the Constitution of India guarantees that a person arrested must be informed of the grounds of their arrest and has the right to consult a legal practitioner [Source 1] [Source 2].
- Article 22(2) of the Constitution of India mandates that a person arrested and detained in custody must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of their arrest [Source 1] [Source 2].

## Important limits

- Article 22(3) of the Constitution excludes persons arrested or detained under any law providing for preventive detention from these protections [Source 1] [Source 2].
- Article 22(3) of the Constitution excludes persons arrested or detained under any law providing for preventive detention from this requirement [Source 1] [Source 2].

## Direct answer

Yes, the police are allowed to handcuff a person under certain conditions [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3].

## Why this is the legal position

- Section 43(3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 allows the use of handcuffs during arrest in specific cases [Source 1].
- The Supreme Court has mandated that handcuffing must be used only in accordance with the law and with due regard for the dignity of the person [Source 2].
- Model Prison Manual 2016 states that handcuffing should be used only when there is no other reasonable way to prevent escape [Source 3].

## How this applies to you

- Handcuffing is permitted if the person is a habitual offender, escaped from custody, or has committed serious crimes like murder, rape, or drug-related offenses [Source 1].
- Handcuffing should be avoided unless there is a reasonable fear of escape or resistance during arrest [Source 2].
- Handcuffing is not allowed during transit to court unless there is a risk of escape or resistance [Source 3].

## What you can do now

1. If a person is handcuffed without justification, they may report the incident to a higher police authority or a judicial magistrate [Source 1].

Yes, a person who cannot afford a lawyer can get one free in certain situations, especially in criminal cases [Source 1] [Source 2].

Free legal aid is also available in prisons through legal aid clinics and jail visiting advocates [Source 3].

- The right to free legal aid is a constitutional right under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution [Source 1].
- Legal aid clinics and jail visiting advocates are mandated to provide free legal services to inmates [Source 3].

- This right applies to accused persons who are unable to engage a lawyer due to poverty, indigence, or other similar reasons [Source 1].
- Inmates can seek aid from these advocates to file bail applications, appeals, or other legal documents [Source 3].

## Direct answer

A person in prison retains the right to human dignity, including the right to be treated as a human being and to be free from physical or mental abuse [Source 1] [Source 2].

Prisoners have the right to basic minimum needs, such as adequate food, medical care, clean water, and hygienic living conditions [Source 1] [Source 3].

Prisoners have the right to communicate with the outside world, including the right to receive visits and to access information about the outside world [Source 1].

Prisoners have the right to access legal information and to be represented by a lawyer of their choice [Source 1].

Prisoners have the right to work, but not to be subjected to forced labor, and they are entitled to fair wages for their work [Source 3].

Prisoners have the right to protest or complain if they are subjected to unfair treatment or if their rights are violated [Source 3].

## Why this is the legal position

- The Supreme Court of India has affirmed that prisoners are persons and retain all human rights within the limitations of imprisonment [Source 2] [Source 4].

## How this applies to you

- This means that even while in prison, a person is entitled to the same fundamental rights as any other citizen, except those that are necessarily lost due to confinement [Source 2] [Source 4].

## Direct answer

Yes, a victim of crime in India can receive compensation through a scheme established by the State Government in coordination with the Central Government [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3].

## Why this is the legal position

- Section 357-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) mandates that every State Government prepare a scheme for providing funds for compensation to victims of crime [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3].

## How this applies to you

- This applies to victims who have suffered loss or injury as a result of a crime and require rehabilitation, including dependents of victims who have died or become incapacitated [Source 1] [Source 3] [Source 4].

## What you can do now

1. The victim or their dependents should apply to the District Legal Service Authority or the State Legal Service Authority for compensation after a court recommendation [Source 2] [Source 3].
2. If the case ends in acquittal or discharge, the victim may still apply for compensation if rehabilitation is needed [Source 2] [Source 3].
3. In cases where the offender is not identified, the victim or their dependents may directly apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority for compensation [Source 3].

## Important limits

- The exact quantum of compensation and the procedure for its disbursement may vary depending on the scheme prepared by the State Government [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3].
- The compensation is not available in cases where the victim has not suffered physical or mental injury, or where the loss is not recoverable in a civil court [Source 5] [Source 6].
